## Results on the electricity stream

Brier score is the mean squared gap between forecast and outcome;
lower is better. Change is relative to the uncalibrated model.
State is the calibrator's saved (serialized) size. Update time is the
95th-percentile time to learn from one batch of up to 336 labels.

| Method | Brier | Change vs. uncalibrated | State | Update ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **streamcal** (20 bins, decay 0.5, prior 1) | 0.178 | −51% | 1.3 KB | 1.3 |
| Sigmoid, refit on recent window (last 336) | 0.179 | −51% | 6.2 KB | 5.1 |
| Isotonic, refit on recent window (last 336) | 0.182 | −50% | 6.2 KB | 0.9 |
| **streamcal** (20 bins, decay 0.5, prior 10) | 0.185 | −49% | 1.3 KB | 1.0 |
| Online logistic regression | 0.201 | −45% | 702 B | 3.4 |
| Isotonic, refit on all history | 0.218 | −40% | 569 KB | 8.2 |
| Sigmoid, refit on all history | 0.227 | −38% | 567 KB | 17 |
| Temperature, refit on recent window (last 336) | 0.245 | −33% | 6.2 KB | 4.0 |
| Temperature, refit on all history | 0.254 | −30% | 567 KB | 25 |
| Sigmoid, fit once, never updated | 0.285 | −22% | 958 B | <0.1 |
| Isotonic, fit once, never updated | 0.323 | −11% | 1.4 KB | <0.1 |
| Temperature, fit once, never updated | 0.330 | −9.4% | 941 B | <0.1 |
| Uncalibrated | 0.364 | — | 54 B | <0.1 |

## Streamcal against each alternative

Using **streamcal** (20 bins, decay 0.5, prior 1) instead of each alternative. A negative
change means streamcal's Brier score is lower (better), as a
percentage of the alternative's score. The range is a 95% interval
from a block bootstrap that respects the order of the stream.

| Instead of | Brier change | 95% interval | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Uncalibrated | −51% | −63% to −39% | streamcal better |
| Temperature, fit once, never updated | −46% | −57% to −36% | streamcal better |
| Isotonic, fit once, never updated | −45% | −59% to −31% | streamcal better |
| Sigmoid, fit once, never updated | −38% | −48% to −27% | streamcal better |
| Temperature, refit on all history | −30% | −34% to −26% | streamcal better |
| Temperature, refit on recent window (last 336) | −27% | −32% to −23% | streamcal better |
| Sigmoid, refit on all history | −22% | −28% to −15% | streamcal better |
| Isotonic, refit on all history | −19% | −26% to −11% | streamcal better |
| Online logistic regression | −11% | −17% to −5.5% | streamcal better |
| Isotonic, refit on recent window (last 336) | −2.2% | −5.9% to +2.1% | no clear difference |
| Sigmoid, refit on recent window (last 336) | −0.5% | −3.7% to +3.1% | no clear difference |

Each interval is for one comparison on its own; they are not
adjusted for making eleven at once. “No clear difference” means the
data cannot separate the two, not that they are equivalent.

## Choosing under a budget

`TradeoffReport.select` picks the most accurate method that fits a
latency and memory budget, using only validation data. The last
column re-checks the budget on the test period, where timings can
differ from validation.

| Optimizing | Update budget | Memory budget | Chosen | Test score | Budget held on test? |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| Brier | 0.1 ms | 2.0 KB | Uncalibrated | 0.364 | yes |
| Brier | 1 ms | 64 KB | **streamcal** (20 bins, decay 0.5, prior 10) | 0.185 | no (1.01 ms) |
| Brier | 100 ms | 64 KB | Online logistic regression | 0.201 | yes |
| Calibration error | 0.1 ms | 2.0 KB | Uncalibrated | 0.381 | yes |
| Calibration error | 1 ms | 64 KB | **streamcal** (20 bins, decay 0.5, prior 10) | 0.069 | no (1.01 ms) |
| Calibration error | 100 ms | 64 KB | Online logistic regression | 0.115 | yes |

## Simulations with a known answer

In simulated streams the true probability is known, so each method's
error can be measured directly: the typical distance between its
forecast and the true probability, in percentage points (root mean
squared, averaged over three seeds). Lower is better. The same
settings are used in every scenario.

| Scenario | Uncalibrated | streamcal | Rolling isotonic | Online logistic |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Already calibrated | 0.0 | 5.1 | 7.4 | 6.9 |
| Miscalibrated, stable | 19.4 | 5.6 | 7.6 | 10.2 |
| Sudden shift | 19.3 | 11.8 | 12.3 | 16.0 |
| Gradual drift | 11.5 | 6.7 | 8.1 | 9.8 |
| Only 1 in 10 labels seen | 19.4 | 10.5 | 11.9 | 24.2 |
| Labels arrive late | 19.3 | 15.1 | 16.7 | 20.3 |

Late labels arrive between 0 and 399 events after their forecast.

## Resource use in isolation

Each method run alone in a fresh process on 10,000 observations in
batches of 100 (median of two runs). Rolling and accumulating methods
refit every 16 batches here.

| Method | Array state | Saved size | Whole process | Predict ms | Update ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| streamcal | 808 B | 1.3 KB | 162 MB | <0.1 | 1.4 |
| Rolling isotonic | 6.0 KB | 6.3 KB | 162 MB | 0.2 | 0.5 |
| Isotonic, all history | 160 KB | 159 KB | 162 MB | 0.2 | 1.5 |
| Online logistic regression | 0 B | 702 B | 161 MB | 0.8 | 1.1 |

Online logistic regression keeps its state in Python dictionaries,
which the array count does not see; its saved size does. The
whole-process figure is dominated by Python and its libraries,
which is why it barely differs between methods. Times are 95th
percentiles per call.
